final_proof:
Let \(Q=(X,Y)=\operatorname{pr}_{M,N}(P)\). By the definition of projection on \(M\) along \(N\), the point \(Q\) lies on \(M\), and the vector \(Q-P\) is parallel to \(N\). Since \(M\) and \(N\) are distinct lines through the origin, they cannot be parallel: two parallel lines through the same point coincide. Therefore the line through \(P\) parallel to \(N\) meets \(M\) in exactly one point, so it suffices in each case to solve the two equations describing these lines.

We use the standard direction-angle convention \(0\leq\theta,\phi<\pi\). Thus a line through the origin with direction angle \(\alpha\neq\pi/2\) is the nonvertical line \(Y=X\tan\alpha\), while the line with direction angle \(\pi/2\) is vertical.

First suppose \(\theta=\pi/2\). Then \(M\) is the line \(X=0\). Because \(N\neq M\), we have \(\phi\neq\pi/2\), so \(N\) has slope \(\tan\phi\). The line through \(P=(x,y)\) parallel to \(N\) consequently has equation
\[
Y-y=\tan\phi\,(X-x).
\]
At its intersection with \(M\), \(X=0\), and the equation gives \(Y=y-x\tan\phi\). Hence
\[
Q=(0,\,y-x\tan\phi).
\]

Next suppose \(\phi=\pi/2\). Then \(N\) is vertical. Since \(M\neq N\), we have \(\theta\neq\pi/2\), and \(M\) has equation \(Y=X\tan\theta\). The line through \(P\) parallel to \(N\) is \(X=x\). Its unique intersection with \(M\) is therefore
\[
Q=(x,\,x\tan\theta).
\]

Finally, suppose neither \(\theta\) nor \(\phi\) equals \(\pi/2\). The two lines whose intersection defines \(Q\) then have equations
\[
M:\quad Y=X\tan\theta,
\qquad
P+N:\quad Y-y=\tan\phi\,(X-x).
\]
Furthermore, \(\tan\theta\neq\tan\phi\). Indeed, equality would give \(M\) and \(N\) the same finite slope; because both pass through the origin, they would then coincide, contrary to the hypothesis. Substitution of \(Y=X\tan\theta\) into the second line equation yields
\[
X\tan\theta-y=X\tan\phi-x\tan\phi.
\]
Thus
\[
X=\frac{x\tan\phi-y}{\tan\phi-\tan\theta}
 =\frac{x\tan\phi}{\tan\phi-\tan\theta}
  -\frac{y}{\tan\phi-\tan\theta}.
\]
Since \(Y=X\tan\theta\), we also obtain
\[
Y=\frac{x\tan\theta\tan\phi-y\tan\theta}{\tan\phi-\tan\theta}
 =\frac{y\tan\theta}{\tan\theta-\tan\phi}
  -\frac{x\tan\theta\tan\phi}{\tan\theta-\tan\phi}.
\]
These are precisely the two coordinates displayed in the third case. Together with the two vertical cases, this proves the asserted piecewise formula.
